title: Rate-Splitting Multiple Access: Fundamentals, Survey, and Future Research Trends
domain: Multiple Access, Rate-Splitting, Interference Management, 6G PHY Layer
abstract_summary: First holistic tutorial and survey on Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) as a general, powerful, and robust framework for non-orthogonal transmission, multiple access, and interference management in 6G wireless networks. Covers information-theoretic foundations, communication-theoretic designs, PHY layer architecture, and applications to 17 enabling technologies.

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.purpose: Motivate RSMA as 6G PHY layer paradigm, compare with existing MA schemes

section_flow.title: Principles of RSMA
section_flow.purpose: Define RSMA frameworks for downlink, uplink, and multi-cell scenarios

section_flow.title: Information-Theoretic Background and Milestones
section_flow.purpose: Trace RSMA roots in network information theory

section_flow.title: Communication-Theoretic Background of RSMA
section_flow.purpose: Resource allocation, precoder design, and system optimization

section_flow.title: RSMA PHY Layer Design
section_flow.purpose: Finite constellation, polar codes, AMC, and practical transceiver architecture

section_flow.title: Comparison of Multiple Access Schemes
section_flow.purpose: Comprehensive comparison of RSMA vs OMA/SDMA/NOMA in framework, complexity, performance

section_flow.title: Emerging Applications, Challenges, and Future Research Trends
section_flow.purpose: 17 enabling technologies and research directions for 6G

section_flow.title: Conclusion
section_flow.purpose: Summarize RSMA benefits and research opportunities

key_findings: RSMA is a universal MA scheme subsuming OMA, SDMA, NOMA, and multicasting
RSMA achieves optimal DoF region in MISO BC with imperfect CSIT
1-layer RS provides best complexity-performance tradeoff with single SIC layer
RSMA is robust to CSIT uncertainties from quantization, mobility, and pilot contamination

writing_recipes.name: Triple Reference Table Foundation
writing_recipes.description: Opening the survey with three foundational reference tables: Acronym List (Table I), Notation Reference (Table III), and Paper Organization Outline (Table II) to establish comprehensive reader scaffolding.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Provides instant accessibility for readers at any expertise level, enabling quick lookup and establishing the paper's scope upfront

structure: Table I: Acronyms and abbreviations (A-Z organized)
Table II: Paper organization with section descriptions
Table III: Mathematical notation with definitions
template.placement: After abstract, before Section I body text

examples: Tables I, II, III positioned as frontmatter before introduction prose

writing_recipes.name: Scheme-by-Scheme Taxonomy with Quantitative Complexity Metrics
writing_recipes.description: Presenting the taxonomy of related schemes (1-layer RS, 2-layer HRS, Generalized RS, RS-CMD, DPCRS, THPRS) with systematic quantitative comparison including encoding complexity, SIC layers, and decoding operations.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Enables readers to immediately understand scheme relationships and make informed tradeoff decisions based on exact complexity numbers

structure: Individual scheme description with transmitter/receiver diagrams
Table V: Side-by-side comparison with columns for encoding complexity, SIC layers, decoding order complexity
Remark blocks highlighting when each scheme is most applicable

examples: Table V comparing 7 RSMA schemes across 5 complexity dimensions

writing_recipes.name: Dual Information-Theoretic and Communication-Theoretic Literature Division
writing_recipes.description: Explicitly partitioning the literature review into two complementary perspectives: information-theoretic (capacity, DoF, fundamental limits) and communication-theoretic (resource allocation, practical algorithms, finite SNR performance).
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Establishes intellectual depth while maintaining practical relevance, appealing to both theorists and system designers

structure: Section III: Information-Theoretic Background (historical milestones, DoF analysis, capacity results)
Section IV: Communication-Theoretic Background (precoder design, power allocation, rate optimization)
Table VI: Information-theoretic literature by year and metric (DoF, GDoF, capacity)
Table VII: Communication-theoretic literature by year, CSIT condition, and KPI

examples: Sections III and IV with Tables VI-VII providing complementary literature perspectives

writing_recipes.name: MA Scheme Framework Comparison Matrix
writing_recipes.description: Creating a comprehensive comparison matrix (Table VIII) that systematically contrasts all MA schemes across design principles, decoder architecture, ideal deployment scenarios, and network load suitability.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Provides authoritative positioning statement showing RSMA's universal applicability compared to specialized alternatives
examples: Table VIII showing RSMA as universally applicable across all dimensions

writing_recipes.name: Structured Advantages-Disadvantages Enumeration
writing_recipes.description: Presenting a balanced assessment with named bullet points for advantages (Universality, Flexibility, Robustness, Higher SE, Higher EE, Enhanced QoS, Lower Complexity, Coverage Extension, Low Latency) and disadvantages (SIC requirement, Higher encoding complexity, Higher signaling burden, Higher optimization burden).
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Builds credibility through balanced analysis while clearly establishing net positive value proposition
examples: Section VI.D (9 advantages) and VI.E (4 disadvantages)

writing_recipes.name: 17-Application Future Directions Enumeration with Challenges-and-Future-Work Pattern
writing_recipes.description: Systematically covering 17 enabling technologies, each with consistent structure: technology overview, RSMA application summary, 'Challenges and future work' subsection identifying open problems.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Provides exhaustive coverage of research landscape while identifying specific actionable research opportunities for each application domain

per_application_structure: RSMA application survey (existing works with citations)
*Challenges and future work:* Open problems in bullet/paragraph form
template.literature_table: Table XII summarizing ~80 references by application and year

examples: Section VII.B covering Massive MIMO through IRS-aided Communications

writing_recipes.name: Standardization Pathway Discussion with Visual Roadmap
writing_recipes.description: Including a dedicated subsection on standardization (Section VII.C) with a visual figure (Fig. 33) showing how existing 3GPP mechanisms (MU-MIMO, CoMP, MBS, NAICS, MUST) provide pathways to RSMA integration.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Bridges academic research to industry adoption, enhancing paper's practical impact and relevance to standards community

structure: Key topics for standardization (HARQ, signaling, system-level performance)
Existing 3GPP mechanisms that support RSMA components
Visual pathway diagram showing Release evolution

examples: Section VII.C with Fig. 33 showing pathways to 3GPP

processing_metadata.notes: Extremely comprehensive 1731-line tutorial/survey with 12 tables, 33 figures, 202 references. Exceptional for Triple Reference Table Foundation and 17-Application enumeration patterns.
